properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Encrypt-then-MAC ECIES: the CBC ciphertext IS separately authenticated — HMAC-SHA256 over IV||ephemPubKey||ciphertext, verified in constant time before decryption (src/decrypt-with-private-key.js:22-26,57-61) — so the malleability concern behind the C rating is mitigated in-scheme, though AES-256-CBC+HMAC remains deprecated vs AEADs. Changeable here (first-party library code).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Published example/test key of the eth-crypto library — intentionally public fixture material, but real private-key bytes on disk; catastrophic if anyone reused it with real funds. The same literal also ships in README.md:84,107,153,206,329 and tutorials/creating-transactions.md:17 — doc sites not covered by this object, reported separately.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test fixture, not production: production code draws the IV from randomBytes(16) (src/encrypt-with-public-key.js:54) unless a caller passes opts.iv, so IV-reuse risk exists only for callers who force deterministic encryption.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum's keccak256 is pre-standard Keccak-256 (0x01 padding), NOT FIPS-202 SHA3-256 — different digests. Protocol-pinned: Ethereum/Solidity semantics fix this digest exactly, so it is observable here but replaceable only at the Ethereum-protocol level; a local swap breaks address/on-chain compatibility. Grover gives hashes only a square-root speedup — not urgent. Identity-derivation security rests on the CSPRNG entropy feeding the hash (reported separately), not on the hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared runtime dependency @noble/hashes@2.4.0 (package.json:107). sha256 from this package is imported (src/encrypt-with-public-key.js:14, src/decrypt-with-private-key.js:14) and used as the HMAC hash function in the ECIES MAC over IV||ephemPubKey||ciphertext. Quantum-safe (Grover gives only square-root speedup); CNSA 2.0 would still prefer a 384-bit digest. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 ships inside the declared @noble/hashes@2.4.0 runtime dependency (package.json:107). No first-party call site imports blake3 — available in the shipped library; presence is what the inventory records (use cannot be proven absent: reachable via config or consumer code). Quantum-safe hash. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 (keccak) ships inside the declared @noble/hashes@2.4.0 runtime dependency (package.json:107). First-party code instead uses Keccak-256 via ethers (inventoried separately as ALG-052c24b2, 43 sites); no direct import of @noble/hashes sha3 in src. Available in the shipped library. Quantum-safe. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key is SHA-512(sharedSecret).slice(0,32) — full 256 bits; Grover leaves a 128-bit quantum margin. See ALG-443012b9 for mode and authentication context.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node's crypto.randomBytes is a CSPRNG — the correct source; the '?' rating resolves to good practice, no CWE-338. The production keygen randomness (noble randomBytes at src/encrypt-with-public-key.js:37,39,54; ethers randomBytes at src/create-identity.js:21-22) was NOT collected by the deterministic pass and is reported as separate findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Primary hash/MAC/random provider of the library, pinned at @noble/hashes@2.4.0 (package.json:107). First-party imports: hmac, sha512, sha256 (ECIES KDF/MAC) and randomBytes/concatBytes (ephemeral keygen, IV) in src/encrypt-with-public-key.js and src/decrypt-with-private-key.js. The pinned version decides the provider's post-quantum posture (all current uses are symmetric/hash — quantum-safe; the library's quantum-vulnerable surface is the secp256k1 curve, provided separately by ethereum-cryptogr
